Excuse me. How do I get to Diocletian's Palace? Am I heading in the right direction?
Yes, you are. Walk along the harbor, toward the old town. It's about ten minutes.
Along the harbor. Is there a shortcut?
Not really. Just stay by the sea. Go past the big hotel and the palm trees.
And then? I always get lost in old towns.
Look for a small gate in the wall, on your right. It's the Bronze Gate. You can't miss it.
Do I go through the gate?
Yes. Go through it and up the stairs. The Peristyle is right in front of you.
Perfect. And the cathedral? Is it far from there?
No, it's right next to the Peristyle. Follow the signposts for the bell tower.
Walk along the harbor and go past the hotel.
Go through the gate and turn left.

Hi Ricardo, this is Maja, from the apartment in Ljubljana. Here is the way from the bus station. Don't take a taxi. It's only fifteen minutes on foot. When you leave the station, turn left and walk along the main road for two blocks. At the crossroads, turn right and go across the bridge. It's the Dragon Bridge, with four green dragons, so you can't miss it. Then walk along the river, past the market. Our building is the yellow one on the corner, right after the second bridge. Call me when you are at the door, and I will come down. See you soon!

Last summer I rented a car in Slovenia and drove from Ljubljana to Lake Bled. It is not a long trip, but I got lost at the first big roundabout. I took the wrong exit, came back, and took the wrong exit again. Three times! In the end I stopped next to a field and asked an old farmer for help. He was very calm. He said: Go back to the roundabout, go around it, and take the second exit. Then go straight on for five kilometers, past a small white church. At the signpost for Bled, turn left. I followed every word, and twenty minutes later I was at the lake. Sometimes the best map is a person.

First Ricardo got off the ferry and asked a woman for the way to the palace. Then he walked along the harbor, toward the old town. After that he went past a big hotel and a long line of palm trees. At that point he saw a small gate in the wall, on his right. In the end he went through the gate, up the stairs, and into the Peristyle.
